gloss: to launch; to shoot up; to hold a wrap-up party

definitions.explanation: To send something up into the air, such as fireworks or a rocket.

definitions.gloss: to hold a wrap-up party; to celebrate completion
definitions.explanation: To hold a celebration or party at the end of a project, event, or performance.

examples.japanese: {花火|はなび}を{打|う}ち{上|あ}げる。
ロケットを{打|う}ち{上|あ}げることに{成功|せいこう}した。
プロジェクトが{終|お}わったから{打|う}ち{上|あ}げをしよう。
examples.english: The project is finished, so let's have a wrap-up party.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
・{打|う}ち{上|あ}げる → {打|う}ち{上|あ}げない (negative)
・{打|う}ち{上|あ}げる → {打|う}ち{上|あ}げて (te-form)
・{打|う}ち{上|あ}げる → {打|う}ち{上|あ}げた (past)

FORMATION:
Compound verb: {打|う}つ (to strike, to hit) + {上|あ}げる (to raise)

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
・{打|う}ち{上|あ}げ - noun form (launch; wrap-up party)
・{打|う}ち{上|あ}げ{花火|はなび} - fireworks that are launched into the sky
・{打|う}ち{上|あ}げパーティー - wrap-up party

USAGE:
Sense 2 (celebration) is very common in Japanese work culture:
・{公演|こうえん}の{打|う}ち{上|あ}げ (post-performance party)
・{撮影|さつえい}の{打|う}ち{上|あ}げ (filming wrap party)
